correctness.rationale: For finite prime set and squarefree D their CRT residue classes on each progression n=Dm+u are uniform by the stated total homogeneous equidistribution: floor f_j mod D corresponds to half-open torus intervals. At prime p the first product coordinate vanishes at exactly ρ_H(p) residues, giving local bad probability ρ_H(p)/p^s. The infinite step is NOT extrapolation from finite CRT: if p divides P_H(n) then p divides n+h for some fixed h∈H. Replacing m=n+h translates one irrational-nonconstant-coefficient polynomial without losing its irrational highest nonconstant coefficient; Holdridge Theorem 1.3 supplies the nonlinear polynomial large-prime estimate, with Champagne covering linear degree. A finite union over h makes the tail negligible; density sandwich yields the product and absolute convergence since ρ_H(p)≤|H|. The source verify.py exact CRT and irrational sqrt(2) finite checks were read. Independent CRT H={0,1}, primes {2,3} computed 7/18, and exact Beatty sample 6437/20000; neither proves the large-prime theorem.

final_claim: For fixed finite distinct shifts H and s≥2 integer-part coordinates satisfying progression-wise total homogeneous equidistribution, one being a polynomial with an irrational nonconstant coefficient, the density of gcd(P_H(n),⌊f_1(n)⌋,...)=1 is the positive Euler product ∏_p(1−ρ_H(p)/p^s); for H={0,1} and floor αn+β with irrational α the product is ∏(1−2/p²).
